repository.name: netwatch

issues.title: [1.0] Make the network health dashboard the primary screen
issues.body:
## Outcome
Establish the dashboard-first UI foundation. Implementation is in PR #14 with passing tests/build and browser evidence; this issue stays open until that PR is merged. Larger-map checks belong to #15; real observations belong to #4–#6.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Open the dashboard by default; keep the existing editor accessible without changing topology IDs or v1 save/import compatibility.
- [ ] Show full-inventory counts for up, down, stale, and not monitored, plus status filters, name/IP search, and a keyboard-operable inventory list.
- [ ] Use a readable primary map, a separate down/stale attention panel, and selected-device details with status, last check, and response time where available.
- [ ] Label sample mode visibly and keep it separate from saved inventory. Actual configured devices stay not monitored until host observations exist.
- [ ] Test missing, invalid, future, and overdue observations. Configured links must not imply measured interface health or BGP session health.
- [ ] Apply UI/UX Pro Max guidance and maintain the solo AI instructions adapted from L.A.R.A.; one owner, short branches, no staging or team ownership gates.
- [ ] Verify desktop/narrow layouts, all status filters, search empty/reset, keyboard inspection, sample isolation, and editor switching; record tests/build/CI and screenshots.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: [1.1] Verify dashboard and topology foundation from a clean checkout
issues.body:
## Outcome
Prove the combined dashboard/editor foundation and existing data-safety behavior. This is a verification step, not a second dashboard implementation.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] From a clean Node 22 checkout, run npm ci, npm test, and npm run build; record versions and results rather than assuming a working developer machine is sufficient.
- [ ] Verify the dashboard is the default, actual inventory is unmonitored, sample data is labelled and isolated, and navigation reaches the editor and device list.
- [ ] Exercise add, drag, connect, selection, keyboard delete with linked-edge cleanup, search, export, and valid import in the existing editor.
- [ ] Verify invalid/malformed/future-version imports are rejected without replacing the current map, and cancelling import replacement preserves it.
- [ ] Verify corrupt saved data pauses autosave, denied/quota-limited writes preserve the in-memory map, and warnings are visible from the dashboard and editor.
- [ ] Record current gaps as unfinished criteria in #2/#3/#15; do not close this issue solely because CI is green.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: [1.2] Finish device editing and accessible inventory workflows
issues.body:
## Outcome
Let one operator maintain a valid, accessible device inventory that can safely become monitoring targets.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Edit existing device name, management address, and description without changing its ID, position, or connections; add/delete continues to work.
- [ ] Allow an empty management address for an unmonitored inventory entry. Validate non-empty IPv4/IPv6 literals and reject duplicate management addresses in the current workspace with clear field errors.
- [ ] Define canonical address comparison and test IPv4, compressed/equivalent IPv6, malformed input, and duplicates. Revalidate at the host API in #4 before any probes.
- [ ] Keep modal keyboard focus inside, close with Escape, return focus to its trigger, and give controls clear labels/errors.
- [ ] Provide a keyboard-operable alternative for positioning and defining/removing links; preserve existing pointer workflows.
- [ ] Verify edit, cancel, delete with attached links, import cancellation, and desktop/narrow use with behavioral/browser evidence.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: [1.3] Finish saved-map recovery and verify inventory navigation
issues.body:
## Outcome
Complete recovery paths while preserving the dashboard navigation already implemented in the pending UI PR.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reuse the dashboard, device list, search/empty states, and navigation from PR #14. Verify them; do not rebuild them.
- [ ] Let the user download the original unreadable saved content before any explicit reset/replacement. Handle storage-access denial without crashing.
- [ ] Keep autosave paused until the user explicitly replaces invalid saved data. Import validation/cancellation never destroys the previous saved or in-memory map.
- [ ] Provide clear backup/import/recovery instructions and show failed-save feedback from either dashboard or editor.
- [ ] Verify empty inventory, no search matches, invalid saved JSON, storage denial/quota, backup, and restore. Do not treat the new recovery UI as implemented merely because save warnings exist.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: [1.4] Verify dashboard readability and larger-map behavior
issues.body:
## Outcome
The primary network map stays useful at the intended inventory size, including multiple simultaneous failures.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Build a repeatable synthetic fixture with at least 100 devices and 150 configured links, using documentation-only addresses; do not probe it.
- [ ] Check label readability, pan/zoom/fit, search, status filters, and keyboard inspection on desktop and a narrow viewport. Verify every filtered link has two visible endpoints.
- [ ] Keep down/stale devices easy to find even when the full map is crowded. Add grouping/collapse or layout changes only if the measured fixture demonstrates a need; preserve manual positions.
- [ ] Display inventory health counts independently of search/filter results. Verify empty, all-unknown, multiple-down, and mixed stale states.
- [ ] Record initial render/filter times, browser, viewport, fixture size, and machine. The 100-device fixture is a provisional check, not a production capacity claim; confirm actual deployment size before release.
- [ ] Save readable screenshots and document observed limits. The existing 2,000-node import limit is a validation bound, not a performance guarantee.

## Validation
Attach fixture-based browser evidence and relevant behavioral checks. No hardware access or live monitoring is required for this issue.

issues.title: [2.1] Add local host API and durable inventory/history storage
issues.body:
## Outcome
Create the real source of inventory and monitoring data. This can start after baseline #1; it does not require unrelated editor polish or SNMP completion.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Add the smallest Node host API bound to loopback by default, with health/readiness and documented start/stop commands. Do not enable LAN or remote access here.
- [ ] Document versioned request/response/error shapes for inventory/topology, monitoring snapshots, and paginated device history alongside implementation; include stable IDs, observation timestamps, collector state, and freshness policy.
- [ ] Persist inventory and observations in SQLite using migrations/transactions. Prevent stale browser edits from silently overwriting newer inventory.
- [ ] Provide explicit preview/confirmation for browser-to-host inventory migration; preserve IDs and links, avoid duplicates, and retain v1 JSON backup/restore.
- [ ] Store explicit per-device monitoring opt-in, defaulting new/imported devices to disabled. Importing a topology or sample must never authorize probes automatically.
- [ ] Validate device types, text/graph bounds, IPv4/IPv6 target addresses, references, and payload sizes at the host boundary. Reject unexpected origins and cross-site writes; keep sample data out of host inventory.
- [ ] Define bounded history retention/cleanup, database backup/restore, and schema migration failure recovery. Avoid unbounded history reads or growth.
- [ ] Test invalid input, concurrent/stale writes, interrupted transactions, restart persistence, pagination, retention, migration, and restore. No live probes are part of this issue.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: [2.2] Implement bounded Windows ICMP checks and health transitions
issues.body:
## Outcome
Produce bounded, repeatable real reachability observations with an explicit failure/recovery policy and useful diagnostics.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Probe only explicitly enabled devices from the authorized host inventory. Never launch scans or probe sample fixtures.
- [ ] Validate IPv4/IPv6 literals and invoke the Windows probe without a shell. Bound worker concurrency, per-probe timeout, polling cadence, and shutdown cancellation.
- [ ] Document and test the initial detection policy: polling interval, timeout, consecutive-failure threshold for down, successes required for recovery, retry behavior, and the expected detection-delay budget. Treat these as explicit collector policy, not hidden UI constants.
- [ ] Keep reachable/unreachable observations distinct from collector/process/permission errors. A broken probe runner must not mark every device down; ICMP reachability does not establish link or BGP session health.
- [ ] Persist timestamped results and finite latency where measured, expose collector readiness/last successful cycle, and prevent overlapping or runaway polling cycles.
- [ ] Test healthy, sustained failure, transient packet loss, recovery, invalid target, process failure, timeout, and graceful shutdown with a fake probe runner.
- [ ] On an approved Windows test inventory, record actual reachable/unreachable results and observed timing. Do not claim real hardware proof from fixtures.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: Add Windows tray controls and optional desktop launcher
issues.body:
## Outcome
Run the local NetWatch host without a persistent PowerShell window, before unattended/remote deployment work. One Windows host owns collection/storage; other PCs will access a shared dashboard URL only after #10/#12 provide secure remote access.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Per-user Windows tray app with Start, Stop, Open Dashboard, visible host/collector state and actionable startup errors.
- [ ] Optional desktop shortcut opens the same controls; repeated launches reuse the existing controller instead of starting another host.
- [ ] Use graceful host shutdown and wait for worker/database lock release; only control processes owned by this launcher. Closing a browser does not stop collection.
- [ ] Explicit opt-in for ICMP collection, with existing per-device authorization unchanged. No sample probes, network scans or automatic inventory replacement.
- [ ] Keep persistent settings/data outside replaceable program files. Preserve existing databases; make data location clear.
- [ ] No admin requirement, execution-policy change, new system component installation, firewall changes or remote start/stop endpoint.
- [ ] Test start/stop/restart, occupied port/database, process/controller failure, duplicate launch and shortcut behavior on Windows.
- [ ] Document interactive session/sleep limitations and the future service mode. In #12, tray/desktop controls attach to the Windows service rather than launch a competing collector; logging out/closing a client browser must not stop the deployed service.

issues.title: [2.3] Connect real observations, freshness, and history to the dashboard
issues.body:
## Outcome
Make the primary dashboard answer the owner's up/down question using genuine host observations rather than sample statuses.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Replace inventory-only health with the documented host snapshot/history API. Keep sample mode visibly separate and prevent its nodes or checks reaching the host.
- [ ] Provide explicit enable/disable monitoring for saved devices with valid management addresses; reflect disabled/not-configured state and host validation errors without pretending checks ran.
- [ ] Update counts, map cards, attention list, and selected-device details from the same observation snapshot; show last check, measured latency, source, and collector connection state.
- [ ] Use the collector polling/freshness policy instead of the prototype's fixed 90-second rule. Age data to stale as time passes even if no new response arrives.
- [ ] Distinguish never monitored, up, down, stale, loading, and failed API requests. Connection loss never turns all devices red; preserve last-known data with its timestamp.
- [ ] Handle reconnect, out-of-order responses, deleted devices, and polling cleanup without duplicate listeners or obsolete results overwriting newer status.
- [ ] Show bounded/paginated recent device history and status transitions with consistent timestamps; never infer uptime percentages from insufficient samples.
- [ ] Test device failure/recovery and API disconnect/stale/reconnect end to end using controlled observations. Keep hardware proof separate for #16.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: [2.4] Add local incident lifecycle and optional approved notifications
issues.body:
## Outcome
Make the first local monitoring release useful for outages and recovery. Local incidents do not depend on SNMP/LLDP or remote login.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Create a local incident when the collector's failure threshold is reached and resolve it on confirmed recovery; link incidents to device history and the dashboard attention workflow.
- [ ] Debounce flapping, deduplicate repeated failures, and distinguish collector unavailable/stale monitoring from device-down incidents.
- [ ] Persist incident opened/resolved timestamps and state across host restart, with bounded retention and one recovery event per incident.
- [ ] Start with in-app incidents. Add external notification delivery only for an explicitly approved destination; keep credentials host-side and offer a safe test-delivery path.
- [ ] Keep delivery timeouts/retries bounded; notification failure must not block polling or lose the incident. Do not enable unauthenticated remote configuration.
- [ ] Test sustained failure, transient loss, recovery, repeated poll cycles, restart, collector outage, and notification failure without sending real messages.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: [2.5] Validate the live dashboard end to end on Windows
issues.body:
## Outcome
A first local release proves the owner's main requirement: genuine network up/down changes appear clearly and recover correctly on the dashboard.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Install from a clean checkout on the intended Windows host and document Node/runtime versions, start/stop commands, approved inventory, and expected polling/detection times.
- [ ] Use a controlled reachable device, an intentionally unreachable address approved for testing, and a device that recovers. Do not unplug production equipment or change device configuration without explicit authorization.
- [ ] Show the full path: persisted inventory → bounded host check → timestamped observation → dashboard count, map card, attention list, and device history. Verify the declared failure/recovery thresholds and maximum expected detection delay.
- [ ] Stop/restart the collector/API and close/reopen the browser. Device history persists; connection loss is visible; old observations become stale without turning the entire network red.
- [ ] Prove map backup/restore and browser-to-host inventory migration without losing IDs or duplicating devices. Test fixtures never populate the real inventory or collector.
- [ ] Reuse #15's larger-map evidence and verify the UI remains usable at the actual intended device count. Record device/browser/Windows details and remaining limits.
- [ ] Exercise local incident deduplication and recovery; confirm retention/cleanup behavior and useful diagnostics with no credentials in logs.
- [ ] Record release evidence and a runbook. Keep the service loopback-only: remote access remains gated by #10 and #12. Do not mark this release proven if physical Windows checks were unavailable.

- [ ] Verify #28's local tray Start/Stop/Open Dashboard/Quit, optional desktop shortcut, duplicate launch, data location and occupied-host errors on Windows. Include visual/DPI scaling and tray-menu pointer checks before release; keyboard/accessibility checks alone are not visual proof. Explain that local mode needs a signed-in awake host; closing a browser/control window does not stop collection, while explicit Stop/Quit affects all clients.

## Validation
Attach actual Windows test evidence for reachable → down → recovered and collector-offline → stale → reconnected scenarios. Fixtures alone do not satisfy this release gate.

issues.title: [3.1] Add SNMPv3 interface collection
issues.body:
## Outcome
Add actual interface evidence after the live dashboard MVP is validated.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Add opt-in read-only interface polling only for configured authorized devices, without disrupting the proven ICMP dashboard.
- [ ] Keep credentials in Windows host-managed secure storage, never browser topology JSON, logs, exports, screenshots, or client responses.
- [ ] Prefer SNMPv3 and make any legacy compatibility explicit; bound timeouts, concurrency, poll rates, and failure handling.
- [ ] Collect interface operational/admin state and counters, record timestamps, and define counter wrap/reset/discontinuity behavior before calculating rates.
- [ ] Show verified interface status separately from device reachability. A device can respond to ping while a port is down; missing/stale SNMP data is not a failed link.
- [ ] Test vendor/OID fixtures, stale/partial responses, credential rejection, counters, and redaction; record a read-only check on approved hardware before claiming vendor support.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: [3.2] Review LLDP neighbors before applying topology changes
issues.body:
## Outcome
Help maintain the map without allowing discovery to overwrite the operator's topology.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Collect read-only LLDP neighbors only from configured authorized devices, with bounded requests and timestamped evidence.
- [ ] Present proposed devices/ports/links for operator review before any saved-topology changes; do not automatically import or probe discovered addresses.
- [ ] Preserve stable IDs, user labels, manual layout, and existing manual links. Define provenance and matching rules for duplicate/changing neighbor identifiers.
- [ ] Treat missing/stale LLDP information as incomplete evidence, not proof a device or cable disappeared.
- [ ] Test partial discovery, repeated collection, duplicates, malformed entries, stale neighbors, rejected proposals, and confirmed application with backup/recovery.
- [ ] Verify one approved hardware example and document unsupported device behavior.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: [3.3] Model verified uplinks and router redundancy groups
issues.body:
## Outcome
Represent uplinks and redundancy honestly. LLDP is helpful enrichment, not a prerequisite for manually configured groups.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Support explicit port/uplink labels, device-to-interface mapping, and configured redundancy-group membership without requiring LLDP.
- [ ] Document the health rule for each group and distinguish device reachability, verified port/link state, and group availability.
- [ ] Do not claim redundancy is operational merely because two routers are on the map; mark missing protocol/member evidence as unknown.
- [ ] Preserve configured versus discovered provenance and manual edits; keep missing/stale interface observations from becoming false link failures.
- [ ] Test a single member failure, all-member failure, missing evidence, stale checks, and recovery with controlled fixtures; use approved hardware for any redundancy behavior claimed as verified.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: [4.1] Add authentication, roles, and audit records before remote access
issues.body:
## Outcome
Prepare the existing dashboard/API for protected access. This can be scheduled earlier if remote access becomes a priority; it is not blocked by network-intelligence features.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Define the single-owner account bootstrap and recovery path; require authentication before any non-loopback access. Do not expose the service during implementation.
- [ ] Enforce viewer/operator/admin permissions at every host API action, including topology edits, monitoring targets, credentials, discovery, and notification settings.
- [ ] Protect sessions and sensitive writes; throttle login attempts and avoid account/session secrets in logs or client responses.
- [ ] Record meaningful configuration changes and access failures with bounded audit retention and safe export.
- [ ] Keep the same authorization rules across local and future remote access. No separate unsecured remote endpoints or browser-only role checks.
- [ ] Test unauthenticated access, cross-role denial, session expiry, logout, request forgery, account recovery, and audit redaction. This security work does not depend on SNMP/LLDP.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.

issues.title: [4.2] Package and verify secure Windows deployment
issues.body:
## Outcome
Deliver a recoverable Windows deployment and a verified secure path to the dashboard, after the local monitoring release and access controls are proven.

## Steps and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Package the built dashboard and host as a documented Windows service with least-privilege execution, start/stop, reboot recovery, update/rollback, and uninstall behavior.
- [ ] Keep configuration/database/secrets outside replaceable program files; updating or uninstalling must not silently destroy inventory/history or backups.
- [ ] Provide a usable restore runbook and verify restoration on the intended Windows host.
- [ ] Keep loopback the default. For explicitly enabled remote access, document and verify HTTPS reverse-proxy or VPN routing, restricted firewall rules, and authenticated/authorized access.
- [ ] Verify failed authentication, role restrictions, transport configuration, timeout/reconnect, and absence of unauthenticated remote paths before exposure.
- [ ] Record the Windows version, actual deployment size, supported protocols, known limits, and end-to-end release evidence. Never deploy the Vite development server as production.
- [ ] Remote deployment may ship without optional SNMP/LLDP features if the owner chooses; do not make them accidental prerequisites.

- [ ] Integrate #28's optional tray/desktop controls with the installed service. Exactly one service owns collection/database writes; tray closure, browser closure and user sign-out do not stop it. Do not launch a second per-user collector over the deployed service.
- [ ] Verify the one-host/multiple-browser deployment: host start/stop affects all clients, authenticated client browsers cannot invoke OS service control, remote disconnects age evidence to stale, and service recovery works after reboot without interactive sign-in.

## Definition of done
Implement only this outcome, update affected documentation and data definitions, run relevant tests/build, and attach evidence. Keep the issue open until the implementation is merged and every required criterion has evidence; name anything unverified.
